title: Learning Rate & Hyperparameters — Change the Pace During the Journey
key_insight: A learning-rate schedule changes the rate during training. Warmup begins gently; decay makes later updates smaller.
body:
## Change the Pace During the Journey

Large early steps help cover distance, but near a good solution they keep overshooting. One fixed pace is not ideal for the whole run.

A learning-rate schedule changes the rate during training. Warmup begins gently; decay makes later updates smaller.

Batch size, weight decay, model width, and dropout are also hyperparameters. They are chosen before or around training rather than learned as ordinary weights.
common_mistakes: The learning rate is the model’s final accuracy.
Hyperparameters are always discovered perfectly without experiments.
Warmup begins with the largest possible update.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Change the Pace During the Journey” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Good architecture can fail when its training settings make steps unstable, slow, or poorly timed.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Change the Pace During the Journey” situation, explain Learning Rate & Hyperparameters without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
